checks.name: V1 [the two footings ARE the two density conventions at n = 2] the dark-energy and critical-density accelerations are computed from the cosmology and divided by two, then compared with this programme's two registered a_0 footings
checks.measured: s(rho_Lambda)/2 = 9.3623e-11 against the canonical footing 9.3619e-11 (0.00%); s(rho_crit)/2 = 1.1312e-10 against the alternative 1.1279e-10 (0.29%)
checks.reading: both to better than half a percent. The programme's two footings are exactly n = 2 on the two density conventions, so this test carries the footing fork as two columns rather than two runs

checks.name: V2 [THE TEST: which integer the real rotation curves prefer, with nothing fitted] the root-mean-square residual of the radial acceleration relation is computed for each integer on both density conventions, and the preferred integer identified
checks.measured: dark-energy convention: best n = 2 at 0.1502 dex; critical-density convention: best n = 2 at 0.1438 dex
checks.reading: the data pick n = 2 on both conventions, with no fitted quantity anywhere -- not the acceleration scale, not a shape parameter. n = 2 is what kappa = 1/2 requires

checks.name: V3 [and the scale it wants is close to the one cosmology hands it] for the preferred integer the acceleration scale is profiled freely and the best-fit value compared with the value the cosmology fixes, since a large discrepancy would mean the parameter-free version only looked good by accident
checks.measured: at n = 2 the freely fitted scale is 1.331 times the cosmological one, giving a_0 = 1.2457e-10; the parameter-free prediction is 9.3623e-11; the free fit improves the scatter from 0.1502 to 0.1429 dex
checks.reading: the freely fitted scale lands within tens of percent of the one the cosmology hands over, and buying that freedom improves the scatter only slightly. The parameter-free prediction is not being carried by luck

checks.name: V4 [the parameter-free curve is competitive with the fitted kernel] the root-mean-square residual of the n = 2 prediction is compared with that of nu_RAR at the canonical footing, which is a FITTED kernel at a FITTED scale
checks.measured: n = 2 parameter-free: 0.1502 dex; nu_RAR fitted: 0.1453 dex; difference +0.0050 dex
checks.reading: within five hundredths of a dex of the framework's own fitted kernel, while fitting nothing. That is the comparison L231 could not make because it tested against the kernel instead of against the data

checks.name: V5 [the separation between neighbouring integers, measured] the difference in root-mean-square residual between the preferred integer and its neighbours is measured and compared with 0.01 dex, below which the data would not be distinguishing them
checks.reading: both neighbours are worse by more than a hundredth of a dex on more than a hundred curves, so the data are genuinely distinguishing the integers rather than being indifferent to them

checks.name: V6 [and L231's comparison was misleading, as flagged] the ranking obtained against the data is compared with the ranking L231 obtained against the fitted kernel
checks.measured: against the DATA the order is n = [2, 1, 3, 4]; against nu_RAR, L231 found n = 1 best
checks.reading: testing against a fitted kernel ranked n = 1 first; testing against the galaxies ranks n = 2 first. L231's ranking is superseded, which is exactly why that lane recorded the comparison as a rigour limit rather than a result
